args.name: Evidence-based assessment of unfamiliar food
args.function: Assess an unfamiliar food source or sample through feasible non-ingestive examination. Distinguish measured findings from unresolved safety and nutrition questions.
args.conditions: Sol has observed mature wild plums and hazelnuts. These observations established visible stock and growing conditions, not edibility. Sol has four roots and five berries as known-safe food reserves and currently has full energy and health.
args.inputs: A visible source, or a gathered sample only if physically necessary. No tools, testing equipment or reagents are assumed available.
args.costs: Specify a feasible method, time, energy, materials, learning requirements and limitations; these are currently unknown.
args.effects: Enable only findings supported by actual examination. If no informative non-ingestive examination is supported, report that limitation. Requesting or learning must not itself certify safety, reveal hidden composition or grant physical benefits.

candidates.effects: Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

candidates.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
candidates.costs: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
candidates.effects: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

candidates.function: Place one or two whole units of an owned food on the ground as a paired exposure trial, inspect their quantity and decay, end the observation or retrieve what remains.
candidates.costs: Start: inputStackId of an owned, unspoiled, nontoxic food, quantity 1 or 2 whole units (default 2), and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: target trial in reach, one round and 0.2 energy. Retrieve: operator only, one round and one energy. Cancel of an exposed trial ends observation at no cost. No supports, tools, water or fuel are used or granted.
candidates.effects: Completed setup places the samples at two ground positions 0.2 apart under the same ambient conditions; with one unit there is no matched control. No food moisture, drying or preservation model exists in this world: both samples keep the existing decay rules, so no treatment difference, preserved status, safety certification or extended lifetime is produced. The trial records rounds exposed and marks a 10-round observation checkpoint; ageing continues while unattended and after the checkpoint. Inspect records sample quantity and decay as a personal unverified record. Retrieve returns only the remaining material, never a replacement. Setup interruption keeps paid work; cancel releases reserved food once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for starting, inspecting or retrieving.

candidates.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
candidates.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
candidates.effects: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

candidates.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
candidates.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
candidates.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

candidates.function: Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.

candidates.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
candidates.effects: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"sol\",\"decision\":\"reuse\",\"ability\":\"probe\",\"reason\":\"The existing general probe operation directly supports the feasible non-ingestive examination requested: observe a nearby source or accessible sample and report only measured findings. Its observe mode requires neither collection nor equipment. No supported examination here establishes edibility, toxin absence or nutritional composition. Related food trials, gathering and consultation add no necessary assessment mechanism; a new food-specific interface would duplicate probe.\",\"specification\":\"Reuse probe (equivalence open-baseline:probe:1, handler open.probe, revision foundation-open@1). Supply target as a currently visible, nearby subject reference, mode='observe', intensity=0; for example forest-plum-2 or start-2-nuts, provided the actor is actually within observation reach. The same operation applies to other accessible sources and samples, not just these instances. Revalidate visibility, reach and target existence at execution; remembered locations alone are insufficient. If necessary, the actor must separately navigate using actual travel time and energy. One completed observation takes one simulation round and 0.2 energy, with no material, reagent, tool, fuel or food cost. There are no prerequisites in the contract, but the actor must individually possess or learn the ability before execution; public registration does not grant mastery. No gathering is necessary for this version. Do not invoke press, wet or heat as part of observation, and do not assume water, heat, equipment or owned samples. Record only externally observable features actually supported by the handler, with target, time, method and evidence-event reference. Existing visible stock/stage information may be reobserved, but labels such as plum or hazelnut and a mature appearance do not establish species identification, edibility or safety. If no additional observable feature is supported, explicitly report that limitation rather than inventing an analysis. Keep visible-state observations distinct from unresolved toxicity, allergens, contamination, internal decay, digestibility and nutrient content; never expose hidden resource fields. Retain the unverified status of personal observations unless an existing verification rule independently warrants a stronger status. The operation neither consumes nor creates material: source stock and owned stacks, including item-4-sol-17 and item-27-sol-127, remain unchanged. It gives no nutrition, healing, detoxification or safety certification. Execution is one atomic interaction, not a persistent experiment. Interruption or cancellation before completion follows probe's cancel rule, yields no completed finding and retains no resumable work; a later attempt is a new paid interaction. Death likewise prevents completion. No spent time or energy is refunded, and no unperformed interaction may be charged as completed. There is no material reservation or material refund. Existing ambient growth and inventory decay continue normally during actual elapsed rounds; no new ongoing process, maintenance burden or physical product is introduced. Review and implementation waiting advance no simulation time. Enforce these established constraints in the existing execution code, not recurring model review.\",\"learning\":0,\"experienceReview\":\"Requesting, consulting, registration and learning yield no experience benefit. A completed observation may qualify only through the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback for personally applicable, verified information gain, including a genuinely informative negative finding; an unsupported assay or generic statement of ignorance is not new evidence. Repeating the same visible finding cannot multiply rewards. Use existing bounded amounts, caps, cooldowns and decay; if no applicable coded rule establishes eligibility and magnitude, award zero rather than inventing one. No automatic pleasure, maintained satisfaction, comfort or nutrition benefit is attached to this reuse. Do not alter protected reward accounts, budgets, goals or permissions.\",\"visualReview\":\"Reuse the existing probe observation event and visual metadata where supported. Each real attempt must distinguish completion, interruption and failure and reference the actual actor, target, method and tick. Any renderer should reuse target appearance and a generic observation indicator, not add a food-certification badge or reveal internal properties. Findings must identify their evidence event; incomplete or out-of-reach attempts must not display a completed observation. This review grants no new visual interface, success animation, inventory item or physical transformation.\"}]}"}
